title: Integral monoid pushout along a submonoid to a group
statement:
Let $P$ be a commutative monoid, written multiplicatively. Its group completion $P^{\mathrm{gp}}$ is the abelian group generated by symbols $[p]$ for $p\in P$, with relations $[1]=1$ and $[pq]=[p][q]$. This is the abelian-group presentation [def-trf-abelian-group-presentation] with generator set $P$ and additive relations $e_1=0$ and $e_{pq}-e_p-e_q=0$, written multiplicatively. Assume that the canonical map $P\to P^{\mathrm{gp}}$ is injective (that is, $P$ is integral). Let $E\subseteq P$ be a submonoid and let $f:E\to G$ be a monoid homomorphism to an abelian group, with no injectivity assumption on $f$. Define $M=P\oplus_E G$ to be the quotient of $P\times G$ by the monoid congruence generated by $(pe,g)\sim(p,f(e)g)$ for $e\in E$, and denote its elements by $[p,g]$.

Then $M$ is integral: its canonical homomorphism to its group completion is injective; in particular it is cancellative. The canonical homomorphism $G\to M$, $g\mapsto[1,g]$, is injective and the action $h\cdot[p,g]=[p,hg]$ of $G$ on $M$ is free, meaning that $h\cdot m=m$ implies $h=1$. For all $p,p'\in P$ and $g,g'\in G$, one has $[p,g]=[p',g']$ if and only if there are $e,e'\in E$ with
$$pe'=p'e\qquad\text{and}\qquad g f(e)=g'f(e').$$

proof.text: The canonical generator map into the specified integer-module presentation preserves products: the relation e_(pq)-e_p-e_q maps to zero. Thus its injectivity implies cancellation in P, by mapping an equality ab=ac to the abelian group and cancelling the image of a. Conversely, for any cancellative commutative monoid Q, map this presentation to the additive type tag of the Mathlib Grothendieck group of Q. Send each generator to GrothendieckGroup.of q; the unit and product relations vanish, so Module.Relations.Solution.fromQuotient supplies the map. Equality of presentation generators implies equality under GrothendieckGroup.of, hence equality in Q by Mathlib Algebra.GrothendieckGroup.of_injective. This establishes the needed comparison with the exact presentation without changing its definition.

proof.text: Define R on P x G by R((p,g),(q,h)) iff there are e,e' in E with pe'=qe and g f(e)=h f(e'). This is a congruence for every commutative P: witnesses (1,1) prove reflexivity; swapping witnesses proves symmetry; for consecutive witnesses (e,e') and (d,d'), take (ed,e'd') and substitute the two equalities in each coordinate, using commutativity. Multiplicativity uses the same product witnesses and multiplies the coordinate equations. No cancellation is used in this step.

proof.text: Every generating relation (pe,g)~(p,f(e)g) lies in R, with witnesses (e,1). The minimality of the generated congruence therefore gives conGen <= R. Equality of quotient representatives consequently implies the displayed fraction criterion.

proof.text: For the converse criterion, the generating relation gives [p,g]=[pe',f(e')^(-1)g] and [qe,f(e)^(-1)h]=[q,h]. If pe'=qe and g f(e)=h f(e'), cancellation in the abelian group G gives f(e')^(-1)g=f(e)^(-1)h. Thus the two middle representatives coincide. This proves the quotient equality criterion in both directions.

proof.text: Use quotient representatives to prove cancellation in M. If [r,k][p,g]=[r,k][q,h], the criterion gives e,e' with (rp)e'=(rq)e and (kg)f(e)=(kh)f(e'). Cancel r in P and k in G to obtain pe'=qe and g f(e)=h f(e'); the criterion gives [p,g]=[q,h]. Commutativity gives right cancellation. Apply Step 1 to this cancellative monoid M to conclude that its canonical map into the specified presentation is injective.

proof.text: If [1,g]=[1,h], the criterion gives e'=e in P, hence in the submonoid E, and g f(e)=h f(e); cancel f(e). If [1,a][p,g]=[p,g], it gives pe'=pe and (ag)f(e)=g f(e'). Cancel p in P to get e'=e, then cancel g f(e) in G to conclude a=1. These are injectivity of the group map and freeness of its action.
